title: Gravity and Machine
premise: Tamsin Whitlock has spent twelve years hauling cargo through contested orbits, hiding the fact that she is a copy — one of the 'backups' grown from the minds of the war's original navigators and stored in her ship's hold. When the Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember futures that haven't happened yet, Tamsin realizes they were sent by the originals as proof that time can be rewritten. The child-captain entrusts her with a message that could end the war by exposing both governments' complicity in the backup program — but delivering it means revealing what Tamsin is, betraying the found family of her crew, and choosing between loyalty to the people who made her feel real and the truth that could free every sleeping copy. In the end, Tamsin broadcasts the message herself, sacrificing her anonymity; the war stalls, the backups wake, and she finally goes home to a family that chose her knowing everything.
about_author: Wren Nystrom is a former merchant marine radio operator who writes science fiction about people who keep systems running while history happens somewhere else. They live in a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, like cargo.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine haul through contested orbit goes wrong when customs officers nearly board the Perihelion and discover the sealed hold. Tamsin deflects them, but we learn what she's hiding: forty-one backup bodies, copies of the war's greatest navigators, asleep in cryo. Emotional beat: the cost of secrecy and the tenderness she feels toward the sleepers.

chapters.title: The Meridian Comes Home
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The deep-space ship Meridian docks at Ceres Station after thirty years away — carrying a crew of children with adult memories. One of them, a girl called Captain Ilsa, asks for Tamsin Whitlock by name, though they've never met. Emotional beat: dread curdling into recognition; Tamsin's past is calling.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The child-crew explains: the originals aged backward during an experimental jump, and they remember a future in which Tamsin delivers a message that ends the war. Ilsa shows Tamsin a memory only the real navigator would know — proving Tamsin is a copy too. Emotional beat: identity shattered; found family tested at the root.

chapters.title: What the Hold Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confesses to her crew — engineer Dov and medic Sefa — that she woke herself from the hold twelve years ago and has been running ever since. Dov's fury and Sefa's quiet acceptance fracture the Perihelion's fragile family. Emotional beat: betrayal and the terror of being known.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The message is decoded: coordinates, names, and proof that both governments funded the backup program and abandoned the sleepers when the war stalled. Delivering it means broadcasting it openly — there is no safe recipient. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of a truth no one wants told.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Both navies converge on Ceres hunting the Meridian's children. The Perihelion smuggles them out through a debris field in a harrowing navigation sequence where Tamsin's copied instincts — the very thing she despises — save everyone. Emotional beat: her inheritance becomes her strength.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Dov, secretly contacted by his old fleet handlers, must choose between turning over Tamsin for amnesty or standing with a crew that lied to him. He burns the offer but not before Sefa learns of it. Emotional beat: loyalty examined as a choice renewed daily, not a debt owed.

chapters.title: The Sleeping Fleet
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. They reach the hold's origin station and find thousands more backups — including a body identical to Tamsin, still dreaming. Tamsin confronts the woman she was copied from via recorded logs and learns the originals sent the Meridian deliberately. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cornered above the homeworld with fleets closing in, Tamsin transmits the message on all bands, signing it with her own name and designation. The war's machinery seizes; ships hold fire as the truth spreads faster than orders can countermand. Emotional beat: climax — self-erasure ends, self-declaration begins.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes Up
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating short sections. Ceasefire talks begin; the backups are woken and welcomed by crews who once feared them. Ilsa chooses to grow up again on her own terms; Dov and Sefa stay aboard; Tamsin takes the Perihelion out one more time — not fleeing, but flying toward. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance claimed, family chosen, truth survived.
